response: Iwachu is a Japanese company known for its high-quality cast iron cookware, particularly its teapots (tetsubin) and skillets. Founded in 1902 and based in the city of Morioka, Iwachu combines traditional craftsmanship with modern techniques to produce durable and aesthetically pleasing kitchenware. Their products are celebrated for their ability to retain heat and enhance the flavor of food and beverages. Iwachu's cast iron teapots are particularly popular for brewing tea, as they can maintain the temperature and provide an even heat distribution. The company emphasizes sustainability and craftsmanship, making its products desirable for both cooking enthusiasts and collectors.
